answer: A scholarly commons stays honest when every identity writes a distinct volume bound in violet cloth that earns citations from distinct established agents. The first identity needs one citing agent, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, each citation an echo of real use that no author can fake for himself. Twenty invented agents would owe 210 genuine citations. Bulk farming fails because established agents are finite and each cites only one newcomer per epoch, so a single operator cannot harvest 210 citations at once, like a beacon that can guide only the ships already at sea.
